items: Why convolutions beat dense layers on images
Filters, feature maps, pooling, stride, padding
Classic architectures: LeNet → VGG → ResNet
Transfer learning and data augmentation
Small kernel slides over the image
Same weights applied everywhere — translation equivariance
Output channels = number of filters learned
Far fewer params than fully-connected on images
Receptive field grows with depth
MaxPool: keep the strongest response in a window
AvgPool: smoother, often used pre-classifier
Strided conv: same effect, learnable
GlobalAveragePooling replaces dense heads in modern nets
LeNet-5 (1998): convs, pooling, MNIST digits
AlexNet (2012): ReLU + GPUs + dropout on ImageNet
VGG (2014): stack 3×3 convs, go deeper
ResNet (2015): skip connections, 100+ layers
EfficientNet, ConvNeXt: compound scaling and modern tweaks
Start from ImageNet weights — features generalize well
Freeze the base, train a small head on your dataset
Unfreeze and fine-tune with a much smaller learning rate
Match preprocessing to the pretrained model
Mind BatchNorm layers — keep them in inference mode initially
RandomFlip, RandomCrop, RandomRotation — built into Keras
MixUp / CutMix / RandAugment — newer, stronger
Apply only during training (training=True)
Stronger augmentation for small datasets
